      "name": "Jev-Negotiated Glyph Merger (Tissue Voting)",
      "levels": ["cell", "tissue", "organ"],
      "mechanism": "Partition the character grid into overlapping KxK cells. Each cell is a 'cell' agent that runs several Jev queries on its local text patch: (a) choice over which candidate glyph ramp best matches its local density, (b) noul 'does this patch contain a coherent edge?', (c) score the patch's motion-arrow density on a 5-level rubric. Cells emit typed votes; adjacent cells with agreeing edge-presence noul >= 0.7 merge into a 'tissue' whose state is the union of their patches. Tissues then run a second Jev round (choice over the merged glyph vocabulary) to pick a single representative. No global optimizer: the projector config for each region is grown bottom-up from local agreement.",
      "jev_role": "Per-cell: noul('coherent_edge_here'), choice(candidate glyph ramps), score(motion_density rubric 0-4). Per-tissue: choice(representative ramp) + noul('merge_stable').",
      "hypothesis": "Bottom-up Jev-negotiated merges raise edge-glyph fidelity from 0.34 to >= 0.42 on held-out feeds, and the fidelity gain correlates (r >= 0.5) with the fraction of cells whose edge-noul exceeded 0.7, confirming that local agreement, not global averaging, drives the gain.",
      "cost": "~2000 Jev calls per feed (batched into ~40 requests of ~50 questions each), no VLM calls during search; 3 VLM critics only on final promotion.",
      "beyond_classic_ml": "The projector is not trained by gradient — glyph choice propagates as typed local verdicts that merge into regions, an emergent holarchy with no loss function."
    },
    {
      "name": "Perspective Tournament without a Center",
      "levels": ["cell", "tissue", "community"],
      "mechanism": "Instantiate N=6 'perspective' projectors (brightness, edge, motion, braille, hybrid-A, hybrid-B) as independent agents. Each is a 'cell' view. For any given frame, each perspective asks Jev a typed choice over 'which of the other perspectives agrees with me most?' (pairwise noul 'do we agree on edge count?'). Agreements form a weighted graph; a bounded local gossip (no leader) runs until clusters stabilize. Each cluster's 'community verdict' is the Jev-score-weighted concatenation of member projections. The final projection is the per-region winner from the largest stable cluster.",
      "jev_role": "Pairwise noul('do perspectives i and j agree on this region?'), choice('which peer is most compatible?'), score('how confident am I in my own region?').",
      "hypothesis": "Gossip-stabilized perspective clusters beat the best single perspective by >= 0.05 fidelity (0.34 -> >= 0.39) on held-out feeds, and cluster count correlates negatively with per-frame entropy (r <= -0.4), showing convergence is signal-driven, not random.",
      "cost": "~6 perspectives x ~150 region-queries x ~3 gossip rounds = ~2700 Jev questions, batched to ~30 requests.",
      "beyond_classic_ml": "No global objective is optimized — perspectives negotiate pairwise typed agreements, a decentralized consensus rather than an end-to-end loss."
    },
    {
      "name": "Guided Growth of Edge Glyphs via Jev Curiosity",
      "levels": ["cell", "tissue"],
      "mechanism": "Start with brightness-only text (fidelity 0.18). Each character position is a 'cell' that may sprout an edge glyph if Jev says noul('is there a luminance discontinuity within 2 chars of me?') > tau. Sprouted cells recruit neighbors: a neighbor is asked choice('adopt same glyph, opposite glyph, or stay blank?'). This grows edge chains organically, only where local evidence supports them. Motion arrows sprout similarly from Jev score('is there directional change here?') above a threshold. Growth halts when a Jev noul('would adding more glyphs improve legibility?') drops below 0.5 for two rounds.",
      "jev_role": "noul('discontinuity_nearby'), choice('glyph adoption: same/opposite/blank'), score('directional_change 0-4'), noul('more_glyphs_help').",
      "hypothesis": "Jev-guided sprouting reaches >= 0.40 edge fidelity while using < 30% of the grid as glyphs, versus the current 0.34 baseline at ~55% grid coverage; if coverage stays > 50% for the same fidelity, the guided-growth claim is refuted.",
      "cost": "~50 growth rounds x ~80 Jev questions = ~4000 questions, batched to ~40 requests.",
      "beyond_classic_ml": "Structure is grown by local typed curiosity signals, not by backpropagated error — a developmental, not a trained, projector."
    },
    {
      "name": "Motion-Arrow Recall Repair by Jev Triage",
      "levels": ["tissue", "organ", "organism"],
      "mechanism": "Motion recall is the weak spot (0.27). Run the motion projector as-is to produce an 'organism' output. Then a 'tissue' layer of overlapping 4x4 blocks asks Jev three typed questions per block: noul('was motion present here in the source?'), choice('motion direction: N/NE/E/.../NW/none'), score('confidence 0-4'). Blocks whose noul >= 0.6 but whose current text lacks an arrow get an arrow inserted with the Jev-chosen direction; blocks with arrows but noul <= 0.3 get them removed. A final 'organ' Jev call on the whole grid asks noul('are motion arrows globally consistent?') and vetoes if < 0.4.",
      "jev_role": "Per-block noul('motion_present'), choice(8 directions + none), score(confidence). Organ-level noul('globally_consistent').",
      "hypothesis": "Jev triage raises motion recall from 0.27 to >= 0.40 on held-out feeds while keeping overall fidelity >= 0.33 (i.e., no edge regression), and the recall gain is concentrated in blocks whose Jev confidence was in [0.6, 0.9], confirming triage is targeted, not noisy.",
      "cost": "~256 blocks x 3 questions x 2 passes = ~1500 Jev questions, batched to ~15 requests.",
      "beyond_classic_ml": "Repair is driven by typed per-block confidence verdicts and an organ-level consistency veto — no differentiable loss connects blocks to the final text."
    }
  ]
}

request.content:
We have a working research harness that turns a camera feed (short frame sequences) into plain text ("projections": character art with edge glyphs, braille, motion arrows). A vision-language model reconstructs the scene (objects, positions, motion) from the text alone; agreement with ground truth is the projection's fidelity. We measured: brightness-only text 0.18, edge glyphs following edges 0.34, motion arrows over edges 0.33 with motion recall 0.27, a VLM reading the real frames 0.92. Search over projector configs is noise-limited; averaging three VLM critics and promoting on held-out feeds fixed overfitting.

Tools available right now, all via API:
- TypeSafe "Jev": a SYSTEM-ONE model that answers TYPED questions about any state (text or JSON) in ~150 ms: noul (probability yes/no), choice (pick one named option, with probabilities), score (expected value on a rubric of levels). Many named questions can be asked in ONE request about the same state. Very cheap. It cannot see images.
- DeepInfra: vision-language models (Qwen3-VL, Gemma-3, Mistral-Small), large LLMs (Kimi-K2.6, Qwen3-235B, gpt-oss-120b, MiniMax-M3, DeepSeek), CLIP / text embeddings.
- MothQuantum: certified quantum random bytes (slow on real hardware, fast in simulator).
- Everything deterministic in the projector kernel is byte-exact integer C, so any device reproduces it.

The research vision: go beyond classic RL / neural nets / backprop. Learning as a HOLARCHY of first-person perspectives — cells -> tissues -> organs -> organisms -> families -> communities — with no central authority: a murmuration or kaleidoscope of many cheap viewpoints that see reality from different angles, help each other locally, and grow structure (guided growth) rather than being trained end-to-end. Typed system-one judgments are the "nerve impulses"; expensive models are rare "deliberations".

Propose 4 CONCRETE, NOVEL experiments that can be run THIS WEEK with exactly these tools on this projection problem (we have ground truth, so results are measurable). Each must use Jev in an essential, non-trivial way, name the level(s) of organization it lives at, and state a falsifiable hypothesis with the number that would confirm or refute it. Prefer ideas where many cheap local typed judgments replace one expensive global one, where structure grows, or where perspectives negotiate without a center.

Reply with JSON only:
{"ideas": [{"name": "<short>", "levels": ["cell"|"tissue"|"organ"|"organism"|"family"|"community"], "mechanism": "<3-5 sentences>", "jev_role": "<what Jev is asked, typed>", "hypothesis": "<falsifiable, with the measurement>", "cost": "<API calls estimate>", "beyond_classic_ml": "<one sentence: why this is not just RL/NN/backprop>"}]}
